FIELD REFERENCE

Coarse fishing: fish species, methods and seasons

Coarse fishing targets freshwater fish such as roach, rudd, bream, tench and perch. It describes a group of fish, not one species. Start with the fish and water you want to try, then choose a float or feeder setup. Check the local season and permission before you cast.

Updated 2026-11-19 · Castward

Which fish and methods belong to coarse fishing?

Key factDetail
Common targetsRoach, rudd, bream, tench and perch — Inland Fisheries Ireland
Float approachPresent bait beneath a float in a river or lake
Ledger or feeder approachPresent bait near the bottom; IFI lists bream, roach, perch and tench among targets
England and Wales riversCoarse fishing closes from 15 March through 15 June; check local byelaws
Stillwaters and canalsMost allow coarse fishing all year, but local and fishery rules can differ

What should you know about coarse fish?

Is coarse fish one species?

No. It is a collective fishing term. Identify the individual fish before you apply a size or catch rule.

Which fish count as coarse fish?

Inland Fisheries Ireland lists rudd, bream, tench, perch and roach. Regional group names can differ.

What is the difference between float and feeder fishing?

A float shows a bite above the water and supports the bait. A ledger or swimfeeder approach places the bait near the bottom. Choose the method for the fish and water.

Can I coarse fish in an English river all year?

No. GOV.UK gives a river close season from 15 March to 15 June. Check the local byelaws and fishery permission.

Do lakes have the same close season as rivers?

Not always. GOV.UK says most enclosed stillwaters and canals allow coarse fishing all year. Private fisheries can set their own seasons.
